articles.title: Protests sweep India demanding removal of Chief Election Commissioner
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Nationwide protests have broken out in India this week seeking the removal of the country’s Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) over allegations of irregularities in the electoral process during various state elections and the deliberate mass disenfranchisement in favor of the ultra-right-wing ruling dispensation. On Wednesday, September 30, thousands came out on the streets in the southern Indian city of Hyderabad in a joint demonstration called by the Left parties, the regional Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), and others, to defend voting rights. On Tuesday, a protest was held in New Delhi led by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) General Secretary M A Baby . articles.title: AI’s real crisis: the $4 trillion bet that could crash the US economy
articles.author: Zoe Alexandra
articles.content_excerpt: Is the AI bubble about to burst? Tech giants like Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle are betting over $4 trillion on data centers, chips, and AI models – but the profits aren’t there yet, and the cash is running out. Michael Roberts, economist and author of The Next Recession blog, joins Zoe Alexandra to break down the reality behind the AI boom – what he calls the biggest economic gamble in US history – and who will pay the price when the house of cards comes down. Roberts explains how circular financing keeps AI companies afloat, what Chinese open-source models undercutting OpenAI and Anthropic mean for US workers, and why grassroots opposition to data centers is a reasonable response to hyperscale projects that drain power and water while creating few jobs. articles.title: Ghana swiftly rejects US health deal, calls it ‘humiliating’
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Ghana has rejected a proposed health compact with the United States that would have provided an estimated $109 million in US health funding over five years, with President John Dramani Mahama saying the agreement raised serious concerns over health data, financing obligations, and Ghana’s regulatory authority. The decision places Ghana among a few African countries that have pushed back against new US health agreements introduced as Washington restructures its foreign assistance following the dismantling of USAID. Zimbabwe has also rejected a similar agreement, while Zambia has raised concerns over provisions in its negotiations with the United States. articles.title: China’s rise: from Century of Humiliation to global superpower w/ Ken Hammond
articles.author: Amanda Yee
articles.content_excerpt: On October 1, 1949, Mao Zedong stood in Tiananmen Square and declared the founding of the People’s Republic of China, bringing an end to the “Century of Humiliation” and setting a nation representing a quarter of humanity on a path toward self-determination. Seventy-seven years later, China stands as a global superpower, navigating a rapidly shifting multipolar world order and escalating containment pressures from the United States. Professor of East Asian and global history Dr. Ken Hammond joins Amanda Yee to break down the historical, economic, and geopolitical forces that have shaped modern China’s development and foreign policy over the past 77 years.

articles.title: Prosecutor leading investigation of Cerimedo arrested by Bolivian police, days after facing US sanctions
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: On the evening of Wednesday, September 30, Bolivian police arrested Attorney General Roger Mariaca and raided the Attorney General’s Office in Sucre and Santa Cruz. The police action comes just days after the US State Department sanctioned and revoked the visas of Mariaca and 21 other Bolivians. Analysts suggest that the timing of the US sanctions, Mariaca’s arrest, and the raids, are no coincidence, calling it “political pressure” related to a high-profile case. Mariaca is leading the investigation into Argentine political consultant Fernando Cerimedo. articles.title: “Berlin 4” Lawyer on Pro-Palestine Protest Crackdown & Germany’s Unconditional Support for Israel
articles.content_excerpt: Democracy Now! 's Amy Goodman is in Berlin, Germany, this week, where the crackdown on pro-Palestine speech is shaped by the German policy of Staatsräson , or “reason of state.” The concept refers to Germany's commitment to the existence of the Israeli state in light of the Holocaust. articles.title: Rise of the Far Right in Germany Raises Fear of an Even Wider Crackdown on Migration
articles.content_excerpt: As we continue our coverage on the rise of right-wing political parties across Europe, we speak to Wiebke Judith from the German organization for asylum seekers’ rights, PRO ASYL , about Germany’s far-right party Alternative für Deutschland, or AfD, and its recent wins in September’s state elections. Judith calls the historic wins — won by margins not seen in German elections since the Nazi era — “deeply concerning for everyone who cares about our democracy,” and says that the growing influence of the AfD’s anti-immigration stance over the German political landscape poses grave risks to refugees, asylum seekers, immigrants and ethnic minorities in the country.

articles.title: The economics of U.S. imperialism (part 1)
articles.author: G. Stewart
articles.content_excerpt: T he U.S. economy is undergoing its biggest-ever capital investment boom, driven by government industrial policies, corporate tax cuts and AI data center spending. Profits as a share of the economy are at their highest in eighty years. The stock market routinely smashes records, and the unemployment rate remains near historic lows. Such economic upswings normally spell political success for a U.S. president. articles.title: October 2026 (Volume 78, Number 5)
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: Marking the sixtieth anniversary of Paul A. Baran and Paul M. Sweezy’s Monopoly Capital , the MR editors situates this key work of political economy within the contemporary political-economic landscape. The tendency toward the overaccumulation capital, they explain, represents a shift from the “ generation of economic surplus…to one of its absorption .” In an age of financialization and market bubbles, the editors note, Baran and Sweezy’s work stands as a testament to the continuing necessity of incisive political-economic analysis of capitalism, inequality, and the irrationality that pervading the entire system. The post October 2026 (Volume 78, Number 5) appeared first on Monthly Review .

articles.title: Marxian Ecology and the Critique of AI Capital
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: What is the rise of AI capital, and what does it mean for contemporary work, culture, and the ecological state of our planet? John Bellamy Foster dispels the myth of a “hyperorganized AI capitalism.” As Foster writes: “We are not entering a stable new age…but rather a new, capitalist-engendered global disorder in which humanity, according to climate science, is headed ever more rapidly toward a planetary ‘point of no return.'” The only way out—the only way, that is, to ensure the survival of humanity—is a radical shift away from the catastrophically destructive regime of capital accumulation and toward sustainable human development through socialism. The post Marxian Ecology and the Critique of AI Capital appeared first on Monthly Review .

articles.title: Babylon Burning: Reggae and Black Liberation
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: Christian Noakes explores the deep connections between the Jamaican Black Power movement and the political roots of its renowned indigenous musical genre, reggae. From the history of capitalist oppression in Jamaica and the indelible influence of Guyanese revolutionary Walter Rodney, Noakes provides essential context for incendiary political radicalism within reggae. Musically innovative and lyrically radical, reggae, he writes, was “instilled with a sense of militant determination that was at once a reflection of the culture it came from and a source of defiant resilience in the face of rampant inequality.” The post Babylon Burning: Reggae and Black Liberation appeared first on Monthly Review .

articles.title: Legal Imperialism: International Law and Dependency in Late Imperialism
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: Today’s resurgence in U.S. imperialist interventions abroad and the concomitant so-called crisis of the “rules-based order” can be explained, Luís Eduardo Fernandes argues, through the category of “legal imperialism, which refers to how the international juridical form is internalized within societies and in the context of dependency, colonialism, unequal exchange, and monopoly capital. “International law and imperialism,” Fernandes writes, “do not stand as opposing poles. They are part of the same unity.… Violence is constitutive of the juridical form.” The post Legal Imperialism: International Law and Dependency in Late Imperialism appeared first on Monthly Review .
